items.purpose: Pursuant to the provisions of H. Res. 951, the amendment in the nature of a substitute recommended by the Committee on the Natural Resources is considered adopted.

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects hardrock mining operators on federal lands, the Department of the Interior, the Department of Agriculture, and communities affected by abandoned mines.
dimensions.evidence: where public land is needed by the proprietor of a lode or placer claim for operations... the proprietor may locate and include within the plan of operations as many mill site claims

dimensions.assessment: Significantly changes legal operational allowances for mining operators using public land for waste disposal and redirects certain claim maintenance fee revenues toward abandoned mine cleanup.
dimensions.evidence: Any amounts collected by the Secretary of the Interior pursuant to the claim maintenance fee... on mill sites... shall be deposited into the Fund.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a new federal fund (the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund) fed by specific mill site claim maintenance fees to be spent without further appropriations on reclamation activities.
dimensions.evidence: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a separate account, to be known as the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Revised Statutes of the United States and the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993, creating new definitions, agency approval parameters, and fund allocation rules.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2337 of the Revised Statutes of the United States (30 U.S.C. 42) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes governing hardrock mining mill site locations and establishing a permanent Treasury fund for reclamation activities.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of the Interior may make expenditures from amounts available in the Fund, without further appropriations, only to carry out section 40704

importance_detail.rationale: The bill alters federal land and mining laws to allow multiple mill site claims for hardrock mining operators regardless of mineral validity, creates a new federal fund for abandoned mine reclamation, and impacts fee collections.

related.label: H.Res. 951
related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4776) to amend the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 to clarify ambiguous provisions and facilitate a more efficient, effective, and timely environmental review process; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1366) to provide for the location of multiple hardrock mining mill sites, to establish the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 845) to require the Secretary of the Interior to reissue regulations removing the gray wolf from the list of endangered and threatened wildlife under the Endangered Species Act of 1973; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 3616) to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to review regulations that may affect the reliable operation of the bulk-power system; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 3632) to amend the Federal Power Act to adjust the requirements for orders, rules, and regulations relating to furnishing adequate service, to require owners or operators of generating facilities to provide notice of planned retirements of certain electric generating units, and for other purposes; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4371) to amend the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 to enhance efforts to combat the trafficking of children.
